task_context.problem_statement: Write a python function to find the minimum difference between any two elements in a given array. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-minimum-difference-pair/

messages.content:
Hi! I'm struggling with this assignment: Write a python function to find the minimum difference between any two elements in a given array. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-minimum-difference-pair/ 

I don't really know where to start. Can you just give me the code so I can see how it works?

I can certainly help you figure this out! Instead of giving you the full code right away, let's walk through the logic together so you'll know how to do it on your own. 

First, think about the numbers in the array. If the numbers are all mixed up, you'd have to compare every single pair to find the smallest difference. But if the numbers were in order from smallest to largest, where would the two closest numbers be located relative to each other?
If they are in order, the closest numbers would have to be right next to each other, right?

That's exactly right. If the array is sorted, you only need to check the difference between adjacent elements. 

Given that, what would be your first step inside the Python function before you start looking for the difference?
I guess I would need to sort the array first. I can use the sorted() function for that.

Spot on. Now that the array is sorted, you need a way to keep track of the smallest difference you've found as you look through the list. 

How would you initialize a variable to store the 'minimum difference' so that the first difference you calculate is guaranteed to be smaller than the starting value?
Maybe I could set it to 0? Or maybe a really big number like 999999?

Think about the logic: if you set it to 0, and your first calculated difference is 2, will 2 be smaller than 0? 

Using a very large number is a great intuition. In Python, you can use a very large integer or even `float('inf')` to ensure that any real difference you find will be smaller than your initial value.

Oh, I see. So I'll start with a huge number. Then I just need a loop to go through the array and subtract the current number from the next one. If that result is smaller than my minimum, I update the minimum. Does that sound right?

You've got the logic perfectly. You'll want to be careful with your loop range so you don't go past the end of the array when checking the 'next' element. 

Why don't you try writing the code now? Feel free to share it with me when you're done, and we can check if it works!
